subject: Media Literacy
title: The Unique Selling Proposition
description: One-minute skill: The Unique Selling Proposition.

hook.text: M&Ms: 'Melts in your mouth, not in your hand.' One sentence. One reason to buy. Billions in sales.

buildup.text: A Unique Selling Proposition is the one thing that supposedly makes a product different from all competitors.

discovery.text: USPs are rarely unique. Most products are almost identical. The 'uniqueness' is manufactured by advertising.

twist.text: Blind taste tests show people can't tell Coke from Pepsi. The 'difference' lives in advertising, not the product.

climax.text: When you prefer a brand, you're often preferring its advertising, not its actual quality.

punchline.text: The product is the same. The story around it isn't.

quiz.question: What do blind taste tests reveal about brand preference?
options: People always prefer the more expensive brand
People often can't distinguish between competing products
Taste is the only factor in brand loyalty
